subject: Connector lifecycle cadence — Catalyst Labs feedback and asks
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@catalystlabs.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Cc: integrations@catalystlabs.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connector lifecycle & deprecation cadence — Catalyst feedback

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Catalyst is evaluating a Redwood connector that powers our 'smart ingestion' product and we have a couple of asks around SDK/API lifecycle so we can commit to the marketplace integration long-term. Attached is a short compatibility matrix we put together (catalyst-sdk-backwards-compatibility-matrix.xlsx).

Top asks: 
- Pre-notice: 1) A public deprecation window that provides at least 12 months of notice before any breaking major API change, and 2) a stability channel (LTS) we can pin to for production connectors.
- Plugin compatibility: if you change model/response envelope shapes, we need a compatibility shim or versioned adapter so we don't ship hotfixes for every Redwood minor release.
- Security & signing: a signed manifest for marketplace plugins so our automated CI can validate vendor bundles before deployment.

We prefer a pragmatic compromise rather than blocking the roadmap — happy to adopt a migration helper if Redwood can commit to a clear deprecation schedule and a formal LTS/maintenance lane.

Can we get your suggested cadence and whether Redwood supports an LTS channel for connectors? Also available to jump on a short call next week.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Integrations
Catalyst Labs

---
Attachment: catalyst-sdk-backwards-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38 KB)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Singh <priya@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connector lifecycle & deprecation cadence — Catalyst feedback

Hi Priya — really appreciate the clear matrix and the practical asks. We hear you and want to make this partner-friendly. High-level options from Redwood: 

1) Standard cadence (default): semver-like model — minor/patch non-breaking within a 6 month advisory window; major breaking changes get 12 months of notice plus migration notes and an optional compatibility shim.

2) LTS channel (partner opt-in): 18 month maintenance window for a pinned connector bundle. LTS would get critical patches and security fixes only; breaking changes would not be applied to that channel during the window. LTS would be a paid/contracted add-on for Dedicated/Private customers or strategic ISVs.

3) Canary/dev channel: pre-release builds with explicit feature flags — good for partners who want early access but will maintain their own adapter logic.

I ran this by Product and SDK engineering — CC'd laura and karthik. Would you be open to an LTS pilot for Catalyst (18 months) plus a migration helper we ship as a small compatibility adapter? If so we can draft a short amendment and SLA language.

If that sounds reasonable, let's schedule 30 minutes next week. My availability: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT or Thu 2–4 PT.

Cheers,
Rishi
Account Exec, Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Singh <priya@catalystlabs.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connector lifecycle & deprecation cadence — Catalyst feedback

Thanks Rishi — that outline helps. A few clarifications from our engineering leadership: 

- LTS length: we prefer 24 months for mission-critical connectors, but can agree to 18 months as a pilot provided Redwood commits in writing to security fixes and one compatibility backport for critical regression.
- Notification channels: deprecation should surface via (a) a public changelog entry, (b) an HTTP response header X-Redwood-Deprecation with timestamp for affected endpoints, and (c) an email to registered integration owners.
- Marketplace manifests: we need signed manifests (GPG or equivalent) and a checksum for release artifacts. This lets our CI gate deployments without human review.

We can accept the LTS as a commercial add-on. For timeline, we need at least 90 days after finalizing the legal addendum before we begin a production rollout so we can update our contract templates and CI.

Proposed call: Tue 10 Aug 2027 11:00 PT (we'll be in SF office) — does that work for your team?

Regards,
Priya

Subject: Re: Connector lifecycle & deprecation cadence — Catalyst feedback

Priya / Catalyst team,

Thanks for the specificity and for being open to an 18-month pilot. We've aligned internally and can commit to the following pilot terms: 

1) LTS pilot: 18 months maintenance window for a pinned connector bundle. Redwood will provide security fixes and one high-priority compatibility backport if a regression impacts your production flows.
2) Deprecation notifications: we'll add an X-Redwood-Deprecation header with an ISO timestamp and publish deprecation notices in the public changelog and to registered integration owners via email.
3) Signed manifests: we will support signed marketplace manifests (SHA256 + signature) and provide a short schema for the manifest so your CI can validate artifacts.
4) Commercials & timing: we'll include the LTS pilot as an addendum to your partner agreement. We propose a 90-day buffer after the addendum is signed before Catalyst rolls to prod.

Action items: 
- Redwood (karthik, vanessa): provide a technical implementation note and a small compatibility-shim example by Fri, 20 Aug 2027.
- Redwood (legal/commercial): I'll send a draft addendum by Wed, 18 Aug 2027.
- Catalyst: confirm acceptance of the 18-month pilot and the 90-day rollout buffer.

I'll attach a short one-pager with the pilot terms (redwood-proposal-lts-options.pdf) and a scheduling link for a kick-off. If that works, we can finalize the addendum and begin the pilot timeline.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partner Programs
Redwood Inference
